For example, you can apply a shaded background on blocks (like this one) to provide a visual separation between multiple blocks. By default, this option is disabled. For text elements (e.g., headings, paragraphs) it is only possible to center the text within a block. In paragraphs, text can also be written with html. However, only a few html elements are supported: a, code, em, i, span, strong

Use the column layout blocks to place content side-by-side. This allows you to place heading, images, or other content next to each other. By default, you can create a section with 1 to 4 columns. Content will be wrapped to the next line based on the number of the columns in the section or they are wrapped based on screen size

Using the page builder, you can create landing pages such as a home page, about us page, or a contact us page. The idea behind these pages is that content is stored in a system of blocks (e.g., sections) and content is placed inside these blocks (e.g., heading, paragraphs, images). This system allows for extensive flexibility in how you create pages as content can be reused in more than one block and blocks can be used in multiple pages.

The Page Builder interface allows users to create custom pages using a drag-and-drop interface instead of writing HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Content can be created directly in the UI and edited using the MOLGENIS web forms. Elements can also be reordered and deleted from the page.

It is now possible to create interactive visualizations inside the Page Builder. This means you can store, manage, and visualize data inside MOLGENIS. The visualization components are built using D3.js, vue, and tailwind. This gives us more control over the rendering of charts and connecting them to our tailwind theme.

In the Netherlands, there are 213 landmarks.

Where does the Netherlands fit in with other countries? In terms of landmarks by country, France, Germany, and Spain have the most of landmarks in the dataset. If we identify countries with a similar number of landmarks, this produces a different picture - the types of landmarks by country that are similar in terms of total number of landmarks. A range of 10% above and below landmark count of the Netherlands was used to identify similar countries.
In this example, we've provided example visualizations using data sourced from The Castle Map (accessed on 25 November 2026).

What exactly is a landmark? Landmarks are sorted into four categories: castles, fortresses, palaces, and ruins (castle maps). Since the definition can vary between country, this categorization is mainly a pragmatic one as opposed to using a system that encompasses regional variations (e.g., language, culture, historical events, etc.).

A number of these landmarks were built in the 13th, 14th, and 17th centuries. This may not be entirely accurate as information about date of construction is incomplete, landmarks may be missing from the dataset, or they are not yet registered on Wikidata.
